page: Amazon Web Services m9g.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the arm64 architecture, specifically the AWS Neoverse-V3 ARMv9 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. There is no local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration bundled with this instance type.

In benchmark evaluations, the m9g.12xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core and memory performance. It achieves top-tier results in single-threaded and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with clang, and static web serving throughput. Database operations, including Redis SET operations and PassMark database benchmarks, also rank in the top tier. Memory performance is highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score and strong cached read-only memory bandwidth, though uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average range.

The instance offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency typical of ARM-based architectures, delivering strong performance-per-resource metrics without the overhead of hyperthreading, as each of the 48 vCPUs maps to a dedicated physical core. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, and the absence of AVX instruction sets may limit certain legacy x86 workloads. This instance is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, database hosting, web serving, software development pipelines, and general-purpose enterprise workloads.
